lanes.summary: GH-4538 makes Σ's corpus walk (`pv_contract::corpus`) admit `crates/*/contracts` (crate has Cargo.toml only, staging excluded), skip byte-identical crate copies, refuse-by-name any stem whose crate copy(ies) add distinct content, and propagate that refusal to bindings that name a refused copy — matching the ticket, the ruling, and infra-83's caveat. Census now counts the same corpus Σ extracts (no more two-walk split), and refused crate-only stems are ratcheted on a new shrink-only baseline (17 entries) mirrored in `check_baseline_ratchets.sh`. Traced the core logic in `pv_contract.rs::corpus`, `code.rs::extract`/`registries`, `duplicate_stems.rs`, `census.rs::census_files`, and the new `crate_corpus_tests.rs`: the admit/refuse/skip decision (`new>0 && new+top_seen.len()>1`) is correct for all combinations I worked through (unique crate-only, identical-to-top, differing-from-top, two-crate-conflict-no-top), and the two prior quorum-round defects (lexical `../` resolution not applied to the refused-binding lookup; `RefusedStem.paths` over-including the kept top-level file) are both fixed with regression tests (`a_binding_that_reaches_a_refused_copy_through_dot_dot_is_still_refused`, `a_top_level_binding_to_a_refused_stems_kept_top_level_file_is_not_refused`) and each fix is backed by a mutation (M4, M5) that fails without it. The receipt's mutation/gate evidence (M0–M5, fmt/clippy/lint/census/readme_contract all rc 0, worktree clean after mutation restore) is consistent with the diff shown. Nothing in the diff exceeds the ticket's scope (legacy/kaizen correctly left excluded; the `../` stem-binding fix is a necessary consequence of walking crate dirs, not scope creep).
